definition.name: Ministry Scheduling
definition.overview:
A **Ministry Scheduling** application is a congregation's serving-schedule system of record: it holds the church's ministry positions and teams as schedulable records, attaches them to dated occasions (weekly services, masses, classes, events), binds identified volunteers to those positions for those occasions, and mediates the back-and-forth — availability, responses, substitutions, reminders — that turns the intended schedule into who will actually serve.

It exists because congregations run on volunteers who serve in defined roles on a recurring calendar, and coordinating them by hand (paper rosters, phone trees, spreadsheet grids) breaks down as the number of teams, occasions, and people grows. The defining core is small: positions, occasions, assignments, and the response loop that reconciles them. Everything else — auto-scheduling, reminders, mobile apps, service plans — is built on top of that core.

When the product's center of gravity shifts to planning the content of the service (order of worship, songs, setlists), it is drifting toward Worship Planning; when it shifts to recruiting and tracking the volunteer pool itself, it is drifting toward volunteer management; when the people being scheduled are paid staff on shifts, it is a different Type entirely.
definition.overview_zh:
**Ministry Scheduling** 应用程序是教会的服务排班系统记录：它存储教会的事工职位和团队作为可调度记录，将它们附加到带日期的场合（每周礼拜、弥撒、课程、活动），将已识别的志愿者绑定到这些场合的职位上，并调解往返沟通——可用性、回复、替换、提醒——将预定计划转化为实际服务的人员。

它的存在是因为教会依赖于在循环日历上担任定义角色的志愿者，随着团队、场合和人员数量的增长，手动协调（纸质名单、电话树、电子表格网格）会崩溃。定义的核心很小：职位、场合、分配和协调它们的响应循环。其他一切——自动调度、提醒、移动应用、服务计划——都建立在这个核心之上。

当产品的重心转移到规划服务内容（礼拜顺序、歌曲、曲目列表）时，它正在向敬拜规划偏移；当它转移到招募和跟踪志愿者库本身时，它正在向志愿者管理偏移；当被调度的人员是轮班的带薪员工时，它则完全是不同的类型。
definition.dc:
The application's world is built from four structures that only make sense together:

```text
Ministry positions & teams (schedulable roles)
        ↓ needed at
Dated occasions (services / masses / events)
        ↓ filled by
Assignment (person × position × occasion)
        ↓ reconciled by
Availability & response loop
```

- **Ministry positions and teams** — the defined serving roles of the congregation's ministry life, held as records that people can be scheduled into. Teams group the roles (ushers, nursery, worship team); positions are what an individual fills on a given occasion. Without these, there is nothing ministry-shaped to schedule.
- **Dated occasions** — the recurring gatherings of the congregation for which positions must be staffed: each occasion carries its own set of needed positions. A schedule is always a schedule *for* occasions.
- **The assignment** — the binding of an identified volunteer to a position at a specific occasion. Assignments accumulate into the schedule of record. They are placed in several ways that mature products commonly support side by side: placed by hand, generated from rotation or preassignment rules (this family serves the first Sunday of the month; this rotation repeats weekly), filled automatically by the system from preferences and availability, or claimed by volunteers themselves through open sign-up sheets.
- **The availability-and-response loop** — the schedule is reconciled against reality. Volunteers record when they cannot serve (block-out dates), are notified of their assignments, respond to them, and resolve changes through the product: requesting or arranging substitutes, trading assignments, or opening positions that others can fill. This loop is the reason the software exists at all; its paper pre-history — the posted roster and the phone call to swap — is the same loop run by hand.

Remove any one structure and the product stops being recognizable as ministry scheduling: positions without occasions is a team roster; occasions without assignments is a calendar; assignments without the response loop is a published list that no one can change.
definition.dc_zh:
应用的世界由四个仅在协同中才有意义的结构构建：

事工岗位与团队（可排班的职位）
        ↓ 需在
日期场合（礼拜/弥撒/活动）
        ↓ 由
排班任务（人员 × 岗位 × 场合）填入
        ↓ 通过
可用性与响应循环协调

- **事工岗位与团队** — 会众事工生活中定义的服务角色，作为可将人排入的记录保存。团队对角色进行分组（招待、育婴、敬拜团队）；岗位是个人在特定场合中担任的职务。若无此结构，则无事工形态可供排班。
- **日期场合** — 会众周期性聚集且需岗位人力的场合：每个场合携带其所需岗位集合。排班始终是针对特定场合的排班。
- **排班任务** — 将特定志愿者绑定到特定场合的特定岗位。任务累积形成正式排班记录。其生成方式通常成熟系统并行支持多种：手动指定、按轮值规则或预分配规则生成（此家庭负责每月第一个主日；此轮值每周重复）、系统根据偏好与可用性自动填充，或通过开放报名表由志愿者自行认领。
- **可用性与响应循环** — 该结构确保排班决策基于志愿者的实际可参与情况：志愿者报告可用时段、接收任务通知、确认或拒绝排班，系统根据反馈调整后续安排，形成持续优化的调度闭环。
definition.rules:
- **The schedule has a draft-then-live shape.** Filling happens on a working schedule; a deliberate publish/finalize step makes assignments authoritative and visible. Before publishing, mature products commonly surface conflicts (double bookings, unavailable people) and distribution imbalances for the coordinator to fix.
- **Availability constrains placement.** Block-out dates and recorded unavailability are honored by manual and automatic filling alike; the auto-scheduler's rules (recency of serving, preferences, family grouping) are configured by the church.
- **Responses create work.** A declined assignment or a mid-cycle conflict reopens the position; products commonly notify unfilled positions so coordinators (or other volunteers, via sign-up) can refill them.
- **Substitution is a first-class flow.** When someone cannot serve, the standard resolution runs through the product: request or find a substitute, confirm the replacement, and update the schedule of record — rather than an unrecorded side deal.
- **Volunteers are members, not employees.** There are no wages, shifts-for-pay, or labor-compliance machinery; the constraint system is availability, eligibility, and fairness of distribution.
- **Permissions are scoped.** Coordinators see everything; team leaders typically see and manage only their own teams; volunteers see only their own schedule and sign-ups.
definition.rules_zh:
- **调度具有草稿然后上线的形状。** 填充发生在工作调度上；一个刻意的发布/完成步骤使分配具有权威性和可见性。在发布之前，成熟产品通常会浮现冲突（双重预订、不可用人员）和分配不平衡，供协调员修复。
- **可用性约束放置。** 封锁日期和记录的不可用性受到手动和自动填充的同等尊重；自动调度器的规则（服务最近性、偏好、家庭分组）由教会配置。
- **回复创建工作。** 拒绝分配或周期中冲突会重新开放该职位；产品通常会通知空缺职位，以便协调员（或其他志愿者通过报名）可以重新填补。
- **替换是一等流程。** 当某人无法服务时，标准解决方案通过产品进行：请求或找到替代者，确认替换，并更新记录调度——而不是未记录的私下交易。
- **志愿者是成员，不是员工。** 没有工资、带薪轮班或劳动力合规机制；约束系统是可用性、资格和分配公平性。
- **权限是有范围的。** 协调员看到一切；团队领导通常只看到和管理自己的团队；志愿者只看到自己的调度和报名。

definition.name: Pastoral Care Management
definition.overview:
A **Pastoral Care Management** application is the church-side system for organizing how a congregation cares for its people: it records who needs care, assigns that care to specific caregivers, records the care actually given — visits, calls, cards, conversations, prayers — and keeps the care moving through follow-up until the need resolves. Its records are treated as sensitive pastoral information, held under visibility restricted to those entrusted with the care.

The defining core is small. Three structures must be present together:

```text
Care need, anchored to an identified person
└── Assigned caregiving loop (named caregiver → contact → follow-up → resolution)
    └── Person-bound, visibility-restricted care record
```

- **Care need anchored to an identified person** — an illness, hospitalization, bereavement, absence, crisis, counseling need, or prayer request, recorded against a specific person from the congregation's people records. Guests and non-members can be care subjects too.
- **Assigned caregiving loop** — responsibility for the need is given to a named caregiver (a pastor, a staff member, or a lay caregiver). The work appears on that person's list, contact is made, and follow-up continues until the need is resolved. Responsibility can be transferred or delegated.
- **Person-bound, visibility-restricted care record** — every care contact becomes a durable note attached to the person's record, visible only to people with the appropriate care role, accumulating over time as the person's care history.

Remove the person anchor and it becomes generic task management. Remove the assignment and loop and it becomes a prayer list. Remove the record and the loop becomes ephemeral to-do tracking. Remove the visibility restriction and the pastoral-confidentiality dimension collapses into ordinary contact notes.

The dominant packaging today is inside a Church Management System — either as a named care module or as care workflows configured over the church's people records. The packaging varies by product; the care loop itself does not.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**Pastoral Care Management**应用是教会方面的系统，用于组织会众如何照顾其成员：它记录谁需要照顾，将照顾分配给特定的照顾者，记录实际提供的照顾——探访、电话、卡片、对话、祈祷——并通过跟进保持照顾进行，直到需求得到解决。其记录被视为敏感的牧养信息，仅对被委托照顾的人可见。

其定义核心很小。三个结构必须同时存在：

```text
照顾需求，锚定到已识别的人
└── 分配的照顾循环（指定的照顾者 → 联系 → 跟进 → 解决）
    └── 人员绑定、可见性受限的照顾记录
```

- **锚定到已识别的人的照顾需求** — 疾病、住院、丧亲、缺席、危机、咨询需求或祈祷请求，记录在会众人员记录中的特定个人。访客和非成员也可以是照顾对象。
- **分配的照顾循环** — 需求的责任被赋予指定的照顾者（牧师、工作人员或平信徒照顾者）。工作出现在该人的列表上，进行联系，并跟进直到需求解决。责任可以转移或委托。
- **人员绑定、可见性受限的照顾记录** — 每个照顾联系都成为附在该人记录上的持久笔记，仅对具有适当照顾角色的人可见，随着时间的推移积累为该人的照顾历史。

移除人员锚定，它就变成通用任务管理。移除分配和循环，它就变成祈祷列表。移除记录，循环就变成临时待办事项跟踪。移除可见性限制，牧养机密性维度就崩溃成普通联系笔记。

当前主流包装是在教会管理系统内——要么作为命名的照顾模块，要么作为在教会人员记录上配置的照顾工作流。包装因产品而异；照顾循环本身则不然。
definition.dc: The unit of work is a care need bound to one person: "check on this family," "visit this hospitalized member," "follow up with this guest." One need involves one care subject; when many people need the same contact (for example, Sunday's guests), the system holds one care item per person rather than one shared item. A need reaches the system by referral (staff or leader enters it), by detection (an attendance lapse or a form), or by self-submission (most commonly a prayer request). Categories — hospitalization, bereavement, new guest, prayer request, and similar — are commonly attached to make care searchable and reportable.
definition.dc_zh: 工作单元是一个与个人绑定的关怀需求：'探访这个家庭'，'访问这位住院成员'，'跟进这位访客'。一个需求涉及一个关怀对象；当许多人需要相同的联系（例如，周日的访客），系统为每个人保存一个关怀项目，而不是一个共享项目。一个需求通过推荐（工作人员或负责人输入）、检测（出勤缺失或表单）或自我提交（最常见的是祷告请求）到达系统。类别——住院、丧亲、新访客、祷告请求和类似——通常被附加，以使关怀可搜索和可报告。
definition.rules:
- **Confidentiality is structural, not incidental.** Care records can be restricted to specific care roles; guidance in the most deeply documented implementations warns explicitly against recording confidential content outside that restriction. In at least those implementations, once a record is restricted, users without the role cannot even see that a contact occurred. Staff-level access does not automatically equal access to restricted pastoral records.
- **The record is the deliverable.** In documented implementations, a care assignment is completed by recording the contact that was made — the note lands on the care subject's record, and the assignment cannot be closed without it. This keeps the care history complete by construction.
- **Open care stays visible.** Incomplete care items persist on both the caregiver's work list and the care subject's record until completed; they are findable by coordinators. Care that is assigned but never recorded is detectable.
- **One need, one person.** Care items are about a single person; bulk needs (guest follow-up after a service) are realized as per-person items so each person's care history is complete.
- **Care attaches to people, wherever they are in the church's records.** Guests and non-members can be care subjects; membership is not a prerequisite for care.
- **Responsibility is delegable.** Ownership of a care item can transfer without losing the record; delegation chains (coordinator → group leader → lay caregiver) are a common pattern in larger churches.
definition.rules_zh:
- **机密性是结构性的，而非偶然的。** 照顾记录可以限制为特定的照顾角色；在最深入文档化的实现中，指导明确警告不要在该限制之外记录机密内容。至少在那些实现中，一旦记录被限制，没有该角色的用户甚至无法看到联系已经发生。员工级别的访问权限并不自动等同于对受限牧养记录的访问权限。
- **记录是可交付成果。** 在文档化的实现中，照顾分配通过记录所做的联系来完成——笔记落在照顾对象的记录上，没有它分配就无法关闭。这通过构造保持照顾历史的完整性。
- **开放照顾保持可见。** 未完成的照顾项在照顾者的工作列表和照顾对象的记录上都持续存在，直到完成；它们可以被协调员找到。被分配但从未记录的照顾是可以检测到的。
- **一个需求，一个人。** 照顾项关于单个人；批量需求（服务后的访客跟进）作为每人一项实现，这样每个人的照顾历史都是完整的。
- **照顾附着在人身上，无论他们在教会记录中的位置。** 访客和非成员可以是照顾对象；成员资格不是照顾的前提条件。
- **责任可以委托。** 照顾项的所有权可以在不丢失记录的情况下转移；委托链（协调员 → 小组长 → 平信徒照顾者）在大型教会中是常见模式。

definition.name: Religious Education Management
definition.overview:
A **Religious Education Management** application is the congregation's education-program administration system: it runs the religious education program a congregation offers its own families — Sunday school, parish catechesis or faith formation, synagogue religious school, and comparable programs — by holding each enrolled student as a record, organizing students into classes led by teachers or catechists, and recording attendance session by session across a program year.

The defining core is small:

```text
The congregation's families (its own people records)
└── Enrolled student of record (a person enrolled in the program for a term)
    └── Class (students grouped with an assigned catechist/teacher and a meeting schedule)
        └── Session attendance (per-meeting participation marks, accumulating as history)
```

Everything else commonly associated with running such a program — online registration, fees, grade levels, rooms, sacrament or milestone tracking, rosters and labels, parent communication — is standard machinery that mature products add around this core. The system is deliberately **not** a school: it holds no academic transcripts, no state reporting, and no academic gradebook. It is also not a check-in system and not a content platform, though it interoperate with both.
definition.overview_zh:
一款**宗教教育管理**应用是会众的教育项目管理系统：它管理会众为其家庭提供的宗教教育项目——主日学、教区教理讲授或信仰培育、犹太教学校及相关项目——通过为每位注册学生建立记录，将学生组织由教师或教理讲授者带领的班级，并在整个学年中逐次记录出勤情况。

其定义的核心是精简的：

```text
会众的家庭（其成员个人记录）
└── 在册学生记录（在特定学期内注册参加项目的学生）
    └── 班级（学生被分配给指定的教理讲授者/教师，并有固定的时间表）
        └── 课程出勤（每次课程的参与标记，累积形成历史记录）
```

其他通常与此类项目管理相关的所有功能——在线注册、费用、年级、教室、圣事或重要里程碑追踪、名册和标签、家长沟通——都是成熟产品在此核心之上添加的标准功能。该系统特意**不**是学校：它不保存学术成绩单、不进行州级报告，也没有学术成绩册。它也不是签到系统或内容平台，但可以与这两者互通。
definition.dc:
Three structures, held together, over the congregation's own people records:

**1. The enrolled student of record.** A person — typically a child of a family in the congregation — is held as a persistent enrollment in the program for a defined term. The enrollment is the unit everything else hangs on: it is created at registration, placed into a class, carried through the term, and accumulates the student's participation history. Students are not anonymous attendees; they come from the congregation's own family and member records, and registration runs through the family.

**2. The class as the taught unit.** Students are organized into classes within the program. Each class carries an assigned teacher or catechist — in practice usually a volunteer from the congregation, with a designated leader — a meeting schedule (day, time, recurring dates within the term), commonly a grade level, a room or location, and often a capacity. The class is the roster: the list of students someone is responsible for teaching.

**3. The session-attendance record.** Attendance is recorded per meeting date against the class roster. Each mark accumulates into the student's participation history in the program — the digital continuation of the traditional class register. Attendance is what makes the enrollment a living record rather than a list entry.

**The domain binding.** The program is the congregation's own religious education — catechesis, faith formation, religious school — administered by the congregation over its own families. Both the students and the teachers come from the congregation's people records. Remove this binding and the same machinery becomes generic children's-activity or class management.
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构，基于教会自身的人员记录结合在一起：

1. 在册学生记录。一个人——通常是教会家庭中的孩子——作为课程中的持续注册学生。注册是挂载其他一切的基本单元：在注册时创建，分配到班级，贯穿整个学期，并累积学生的参与历史。学生不是匿名参与者；他们来自教会的家庭和成员记录，注册通过家庭进行。

2. 班级作为教学单元。学生被组织到课程中的班级。每个班级有一个指定的教师或教义问答者——实践中通常是教会的志愿者，有指定的领导者——一个会议时间表（日期、时间、学期内的重复日期）、通常一个年级水平、一个教室或位置，以及经常一个容量。班级就是花名册：某人负责教学的学生名单。

3. 会议出勤记录。出勤按会议日期记录在班级花名册上。每个标记累积到学生在课程中的参与历史——传统班级登记簿的数字延续。出勤使注册成为一个活记录而不是列表条目。

域绑定：课程是教会...
definition.rules:
- **People come from the congregation's records.** Students and volunteers must exist in the congregation's family/member records before they can be enrolled or assigned — the program administers the congregation's own people, not a walk-in population.
- **Attendance requires a scheduled meeting.** A class with no meeting dates, or not tied to a session, cannot take attendance.
- **Enrollment gates attendance visibility.** In the deepest-documented implementation, a student appears on an attendance list only when the enrollment date falls within the session's date parameters.
- **Capacity gates acceptance.** Registration into a full class can be rejected; in products with an online registration flow, families are notified of acceptance or rejection.
- **Attendance records persist.** Once recorded, an attendance record stays; statuses can be changed (present ↔ absent, tardy, excused) but the record is not removed.
- **Milestone records are permanent.** In the deepest-documented implementation, sacrament records can be viewed, added, edited, and printed but not deleted.
- **Structure in use is retired, not deleted.** A term that has been used in classes or sessions is deactivated rather than deleted.
- **Fees are family-shaped.** Fee logic commonly operates at the family level: per-child amounts, multi-child discounts, and caps on what a family pays in total.
- **Rollover copies structure, not students.** Copying classes and sessions to the next term typically carries the class setup; students move by promotion or transfer.
definition.rules_zh:
- **人员来自会众记录。** 学生和志愿者在被注册或分配之前，必须在会众的家庭/成员记录中存在——该项目管理的是会众自身的成员，而非临时来访人员。
- **出勤需要预定的会议。** 没有会议日期或未与课程关联的班级无法记录出勤。
- **注册状态决定出勤可见性。** 在文档记录最详尽的实现中，只有当注册日期落在课程的日期参数范围内时，学生才会出现在出勤名单上。
- **容量限制录取。** 对已满班级的注册申请可以被拒绝；在具有在线注册流程的产品中，家庭会收到录取或拒绝的通知。
- **出勤记录会持久保存。** 一旦记录，出勤记录即被保存；状态可以更改（出席 ↔ 缺席、迟到、请假），但记录本身不会被删除。
- **里程碑记录是永久的。** 在文档记录最详尽的实现中，圣事记录可以被查看、添加、编辑和打印，但不能删除。
- **使用中的结构是停用，而非删除。** 已用于班级或课程的学期将被停用，而非删除。
- **费用是基于家庭结构的。** 费用逻辑通常在家庭层面运作：按子女计算费用、多子女折扣以及家庭总费用的上限。
- **滚动复制的是结构，而非学生。** 将班级和课程复制到下一学期时，通常复制的是班级设置；学生则通过升级或转班来移动。

definition.name: Religious Event Management
definition.overview:
A **Religious Event Management** application is a religious organization's event-participation system: it lets a congregation (or mosque, temple, or faith ministry) create, publish, register people for, run, and close its events — vacation Bible school, camps and retreats, conferences, classes and workshops, holiday services, service projects, dinners — with every registration bound to an identified person in the organization's own records.

What makes this more than generic event software is that **the organization already knows (or wants to know) its people**. Registrations are not anonymous rows: they resolve to person records in the congregation's database — native or integrated — unknown registrants become records, one person commonly registers their whole household, and what happens at the event (signed up, paid, attended, no-showed) is written back onto each person's record to feed follow-up and engagement.

The boundary in one sentence: when registration binds to the congregation's people records and participation persists there, the work belongs here; when attendees are anonymous and the center is ticket revenue or attendee logistics, it belongs to generic event management; when the event's economy is gifts with a receipts-and-acknowledgment close, it belongs to nonprofit event fundraising.
definition.overview_zh:
一个**宗教事件管理**应用程序是一个宗教组织的事件参与系统：它允许一个会众（或清真寺、寺庙或信仰事工）创建、发布、为人员注册、运行和关闭其事件——假期圣经学校、营会和退修会、会议、课程和研讨会、节日服务、服务项目、晚餐——每次注册都与组织自身记录中的一个已识别人员相关联。

使其不仅仅是通用事件软件的原因是**组织已经知道（或想要知道）其人员**。注册不是匿名行：它们解析为会众数据库中的人员记录——原生或集成的——未知注册者成为记录，一个人通常注册其整个家庭，而在事件中发生的事情（已注册、已支付、已出席、未出席）被写回每个人员记录以支持后续和参与。

一句话的边界：当注册与会众的人员记录绑定且参与持久存在于此，那么这项工作属于这里；当参与者是匿名的且中心是门票收入或参与者后勤时，它属于通用事件管理；当事件的经济是礼物并以收据和确认结束时，它属于非营利事件筹款。
definition.dc:
Three structures, all held together. Remove any one and the product stops being this type of software.

- **The event as the managed unit of work.** An event is a persistent, configured record — name, description, schedule (commonly with multiple date/time options), location, registration options with prices and capacities, and open/close windows — which the organization creates, opens for registration, runs, and closes or archives. Capacity is enforced at the event level and at the level of individual registration options. (Without this, there is nothing to manage — just a form or a calendar entry.)

- **The congregation-registry binding.** Every registration resolves to an identified person in the organization's people records. The registry may be native to the product or a connected church-management database; either way, a registration is a binding between an event and a known person — and a registrant the organization doesn't yet know becomes a new record. One registrant commonly registers other people: a parent registers each child for VBS, a spouse registers both of them for a marriage retreat. (Without this, the product is generic event registration software with anonymous attendees.)

- **The participation write-back.** What actually happened persists on the person's record: who signed up, who paid, who attended, who RSVP'd but didn't show. This history feeds the organization's follow-up (welcome sequences, reminders, next-step invitations) and its engagement picture — the same record core the church management system keeps, filled by the events loop. (Without this, registration is siloed from people's lives — the exact failure mode vendors warn against when churches use forms outside their database.)
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构，都保持在一起。移除任何一个，产品就不再是这种类型的软件。

- **事件作为管理的工作单元。** 事件是一个持久的、配置的记录——名称、描述、时间表（通常有多个日期/时间选项）、地点、注册选项（包含价格和容量）、以及开放/关闭窗口——组织创建它、开放注册、运行它、关闭或存档它。容量在事件级别和单个注册选项级别强制执行。（如果没有这个，就没有什么可管理的——只是一个表单或日历条目。）

- **会众登记绑定。** 每个注册都解析为组织人员记录中一个已识别的人员。登记可能是产品自带的或连接的教会管理数据库；无论哪种方式，注册是事件和已知人员之间的绑定——而组织尚未认识的注册者将成为一个新记录。一个注册者通常注册其他人：家长为VBS注册每个孩子，配偶为婚姻静修注册两个人。（如果没有这个，产品就是带有匿名参与者的通用事件注册软件。）

- **参与度回写。** 实际发生的情况持久保存在个人记录中：谁报名、谁付费、谁出席、谁回复了但没来。这个历史记录馈送组织
definition.rules:
- **A registration is a person, not a row.** Every registration resolves to an identified person record; unknown registrants become records. This is the structural rule that separates the Type from generic event registration.
- **Households register together.** One registrant commonly registers multiple people — children, spouses — in a single transaction, often with a per-transaction limit; per-attendee data (allergies, sizes, grades) is collected for each person individually.
- **Capacity is enforced at two levels.** Both the event and its individual registration options carry capacities; when an option fills, registration closes for it — and in some products a waitlist absorbs further interest.
- **Free and paid events are equal citizens.** Many events are free headcount signups; fee-charging events (camps, retreats, conferences) add payments, deposits, installments, discounts, and refunds. Money is fees, not gifts — giving is not part of the event machinery in most products.
- **Openness is the default posture.** Events are publicized and open to guests; registration typically requires no membership and often no login. Membership standing does not normally gate access or price (in contrast to association event management).
- **Participation outlives the event.** Attendance and signup history persist on person records and feed follow-up workflows and engagement views; no-shows are visible and actionable.
- **Access is scoped.** Ministry leaders and volunteers commonly see only their own events; organization-wide configuration stays with staff.
- **Events are records, not throwaways.** Some products prevent outright deletion of events (closing or archiving instead), preserving the participation trail.
definition.rules_zh:
- **注册是一个人，而不是一行。** 每次注册解析为一个已识别的人员记录；未知注册者成为记录。这是将类型与通用事件注册区分开来的结构规则。
- **家庭一起注册。** 一个注册者通常在一个事务中注册多个人——孩子、配偶——通常有每事务限制；每位参与者的数据（过敏、尺寸、年级）为每个人单独收集。
- **容量在两个层面执行。** 事件及其各个注册选项都带有容量；当选项填满时，该选项的注册关闭——在某些产品中，候补名单吸收进一步的兴趣。
- **免费和付费事件是平等公民。** 许多事件是免费的签到；收费事件（营会、退修会、会议）添加支付、押金、分期付款、折扣和退款。钱是费用，不是礼物——在大多数产品中，捐赠不是事件机制的一部分。
- **开放性是默认姿态。** 事件被宣传并向访客开放；注册通常不需要会员身份，通常也不需要登录。会员身份通常不控制访问或价格（与协会事件管理相反）。
- **参与持续于事件之后。** 出席和注册历史持久存在于人员记录上，并支持后续工作流和参与视图；缺席可见且可操作。
- **访问是有范围的。** 事工领导者和志愿者通常只看到自己的事件；组织范围的配置由工作人员保留。
- **事件是记录，不是一次性物品。** 某些产品防止完全删除事件（改为关闭或归档），保留参与轨迹。

definition.name: Religious Small-group Management
definition.overview:
A **Religious Small-group Management** application is a congregation's small-group ministry system: it holds each ongoing group — a life group, home group, Bible study, youth group, or care/affinity group — as a persistent record with a designated leader and a membership roster drawn from the congregation's own people records, connects people to groups through a find-and-join front door, runs each group's ongoing life (joining, meetings, attendance, communication) largely through self-serving lay leaders, and reports the group picture back to staff so the congregation can see who is connected and who is drifting.

The defining core is small:

```text
The congregation's people records  (the registry substrate)
└── Group  (the persistent community of record)
    ├── Leader(s) + membership roster  → roles, join dates
    ├── Join rules  → open / request-to-join / closed, with limits
    ├── Group life  → meetings & attendance, communication,
    │                 group events, shared resources
    └── The group picture  → attendance trends, drop-off follow-up,
                              health reporting → written back to people
```

Everything commonly associated with modern small-group software — the public group finder, leader self-service portals, group chat, health metrics, coaching structures — is standard machinery that mature products add around this core. The system is deliberately **not** a conversation app (messaging is one capability of the group, not the center), not an event tool (a group persists across meetings and seasons; an event is a dated occurrence), and not the congregation's whole record system (it organizes known people into communities; it does not own the congregation's roster, giving, or check-in).
definition.overview_zh:
一个**宗教小型团体管理**应用是一个会众的小型团体事工系统：它保存每个持续存在的团体——一个生命小组、家庭小组、查经班、青年团体或关怀/亲密小组——作为一个持久记录，拥有一个指定负责人和一份从会众自身人员记录中提取的成员名单，通过一个可发现和加入的前门将人员与团体连接起来，主要通过自助服务的平信徒负责人运行每个团体的持续生活（加入、会议、出席、沟通），并将团体状况报告给工作人员，以便会众能看到谁有联系，谁在疏远。

其定义的核心很小：

```text
会众的人员记录（注册基础）
└── 团体（持久的记录在册的社群）
    ├── 负责人 + 成员名单 → 角色、加入日期
    ├── 加入规则 → 开放 / 申请加入 / 封闭，并带有限制
    ├── 团体生活 → 会议与出席、沟通、
    │              团体活动、共享资源
    └── 团体状况 → 出席趋势、脱落跟进、
                   健康报告 → 写回到人员记录中
```

所有通常与现代小型团体软件相关联的东西——公共团体查找器、负责人自助门户、团体聊天、健康指标、指导结构——都是成熟产品围绕这个核心添加的标准机制。该系统有意**不**是一个对话应用（消息传递是团体的一个功能，而非中心），**不**是一个活动工具（团体跨会议和季度持续存在；活动是一个有日期的事件），也**不**是会众的完整记录系统（它将已知人员组织成社群；它不拥有会众的名单、奉献或签到）。
definition.dc:
Three structures, held together, over the congregation's own people records. Remove any one and the product stops being this type of software.

**1. The group as a persistent community of record.** A group is a named, ongoing sub-community of the congregation — carrying a designated leader, a bounded membership roster, and how and when it typically meets — held as a durable record that is created, maintained across meetings and seasons, and eventually archived or ended rather than expiring with any single date. This is what separates a group from an event: an event happens on a date and closes; a group persists and its life is recorded over time.

**2. The congregation-people binding.** Group members and leaders resolve to identified people in the congregation's own records — held natively by the product or synchronized with an integrated church database. The group is a sub-community of a known population, not an open public graph, and the group's membership and participation attach to each person's record. A seeker who joins a group becomes a known person; a member's group involvement sits beside their giving, attendance, and event history.

**3. The administered group-life loop.** The group's ongoing life is operated and recorded over time: people join and leave under the group's join rules, its meetings happen and participation is recorded against the roster (per-meeting attendance is the dominant realization), the group communicates as a body, and the organization can see and act on all of it. Without this loop the product is just a directory of groups.
definition.dc_zh:
三个结构，相互关联，基于会众自身的人员记录。移除任何一个，产品就不再是这种类型的软件。

1. 小组作为持久的记录社区。小组是会众的一个命名的、持续的子社区——包含指定的领导者、限定的成员名册，以及通常如何和何时聚会——作为持久记录被创建、跨会议和季节维护，并最终归档或结束，而不是在任何单个日期过期。这区分了小组与活动：活动在特定日期发生并结束；小组持续存在，其生命周期随时间记录。

2. 会众与人员的绑定。小组成员和领导者解析到会众自身记录中的已识别人员——由产品原生持有或与集成的教会数据库同步。小组是一个已知人群的子社区，而不是开放的公共图，小组的成员资格和参与附加到每个人的记录上。一个寻求者加入小组后成为已知人员；一个成员的小组参与与他们的奉献、出席和活动历史并列。

3. 管理的小组生活循环。小组的持续生活随时间被操作和记录：人们根据小组的加入规则加入和离开，会议发生，参与情况根据名册记录（每次会议出席），小组被定期评估或报告，状态更新和通信由领导者或管理员处理。
definition.rules:
- **Join rules gate membership.** Each group carries its own rule — open signup, request-to-join with leader approval, or closed — and enrollment limits (member caps, closing dates) that automatically close a group when reached. The same church typically runs all postures at once.
- **Membership is a person-to-group state.** Memberships carry a join date and a role (member or leader); in the deepest-documented implementation a person holds at most one active membership in a given group at a time. Promoting someone to leader can be an administrator-level action, not a leader-level one.
- **Leaders are delegated, not sovereign.** Leaders manage their own groups without administrative access to the church database; access to the whole people database from the group workspace is gated — one vendor documents it as explicitly not recommended. Staff retain visibility over everything leaders do.
- **Confidentiality shapes community.** Member lists can be hidden or anonymous (recovery, grief, counseling groups); in one documented implementation, features that would expose member identities to each other are disabled while the list is confidential. Privacy and community are in deliberate tension, and the group's posture governs it.
- **Attendance is leader-captured and engineered for compliance.** Because leaders are volunteers, products minimize friction (reminder links, pre-checked names, no login) and some escalate — repeated reminders, then notification of staff or the coach — when attendance goes unrecorded.
- **Groups are records, not throwaways.** Groups are archived or ended rather than deleted, preserving the participation trail; mature products support duplicating a group into a new season instead of starting over.
- **Participation outlives the meeting.** Group membership and attendance persist on the person's record beside giving, check-in, and event history — the substrate for the congregation's engagement questions.
- **Children are a boundary case.** Some products restrict children from member-facing accounts and group messaging entirely, routing kids through children's check-in instead; student groups commonly require leader approval so parents and leaders stay in the loop.
definition.rules_zh:
- **加入规则把关成员资格。** 每个团体都带有自己的规则——开放注册、需要负责人批准的申请加入、或封闭——以及注册限制（成员上限、关闭日期），达到限制时会自动关闭团体。同一间教会通常同时运行所有姿态。
- **成员资格是一个人对团体的状态。** 成员资格带有加入日期和角色（成员或负责人）；在有最详细记录的实现中，一个人在特定团体中同一时间最多持有一个活跃的成员身份。将某人提升为负责人可以是管理员级别的操作，而非负责人级别的。
- **负责人是被授权的，而非自主的。** 负责人管理自己的团体，但没有访问教会数据库的管理权限；从团体工作区访问整个人员数据库是受控的——一个供应商明确记录为不推荐。工作人员保留对负责人所有操作的可见性。
- **保密性塑造社群。** 成员名单可以被隐藏或匿名（康复、哀伤、辅导团体）；在一个有记录的实现中，当名单处于保密状态时，会禁用那些会向彼此暴露成员身份的功能。隐私和社群之间存在有意的张力，团体的姿态对此进行调控。
- **出席由负责人记录，并为合规性而设计。** 因为负责人是志愿者，产品尽量减少摩擦（提醒链接、预选姓名、无需登录），有些还会升级处理——当出席未被记录时，进行重复提醒，然后通知工作人员或教练。
- **团体是记录，而非一次性用品。** 团体会被存档或结束，而非删除，以保留参与轨迹；成熟产品支持将团体复制到一个新的季度，而非从头开始。
- **参与度超越会议。** 团体成员
